label: conj:hyperbolic-volume-transcendence
title: Algebraic independence of QOU hyperbolic volumes
html:
Conjecture. Algebraic independence of QOU hyperbolic volumes

The topological mass formula assigns mass \mathfrak{m}(K) = \mathrm{Vol}(K)/\hbar_q^2. Here q denotes the substrate parameter. Three non-zero hyperbolic volumes drive the Descartes universe mass spectrum:

Knot/Link Volume QOU identity
Figure-eight 4_1 \mathrm{Vol}(4_1) = 2\,\mathrm{Cl}_2(\pi/3) \approx 2.02988 Higgs boson
Three-twist 5_2 \mathrm{Vol}(5_2) \approx 2.82812 Down quark
Borromean rings \mathcal{B}_3 \mathrm{Vol}(\mathcal{B}_3) \approx 7.32772 Nucleon

All torus knots (trefoil, cinquefoil, septafoil) possess zero hyperbolic volume. They contribute no topological mass from this channel.

Conjecture. The set \{\mathrm{Vol}(4_1),\; \mathrm{Vol}(5_2),\; \mathrm{Vol}(\mathcal{B}_3)\} is algebraically independent over \mathbb{Q}[q, q^{-1}]. There exists no non-zero polynomial P \in \mathbb{Q}[q, q^{-1}][x, y, z] satisfying

  P\bigl(\mathrm{Vol}(4_1),\; \mathrm{Vol}(5_2),\;
    \mathrm{Vol}(\mathcal{B}_3)\bigr) = 0.

If the conjecture holds, the physical coefficient ring of the Descartes universe forms \mathbb{Q}[q, q^{-1}][\mathrm{Vol}(4_1), \mathrm{Vol}(5_2), \mathrm{Vol}(\mathcal{B}_3)]. This defines a polynomial ring in three transcendentals over the ground ring. The specialisation map \iota \colon \mathbb{Z}[q, q^{-1}] \to \mathbb{R} sending q \mapsto q_0 extends to an embedding of this ring into \mathbb{R}. The three volumes remain algebraically independent over \mathbb{Q}(q_0).

Remark. The irrationality of a single hyperbolic 3-manifold volume remains an open problem. The Borel--Zagier conjecture concerns only \mathbb{Q}-linear independence of volumes of non-commensurable manifolds. This presents a strictly weaker, yet unresolved, claim. Reid (1991) established 4_1 as the unique arithmetic hyperbolic knot, commensurable with \mathrm{PSL}_2(\mathcal{O}_3). The three-twist 5_2 is non-arithmetic. The Borromean rings \mathcal{B}_3, as a 3-component link, fall outside Reid's classification. The three complements are pairwise non-commensurable. The Borel--Zagier conjecture would thus guarantee their \mathbb{Q}-linear independence.

Scope: external open problem, partial categorical approach. This conjecture remains external to the framework. Its three forms

  \text{irrationality}
  \;\Longleftarrow\;
  \mathbb{Q}\text{-linear independence}
  \;\Longleftarrow\;
  \text{algebraic independence}

represent recognised open problems in transcendental number theory. These include single-volume irrationality (no hyperbolic 3-manifold volume is known to be irrational), Borel--Zagier, and the Kontsevich--Zagier and Grothendieck period conjectures. The framework specifies only the choice of the three knots 4_1, 5_2, \mathcal{B}_3. The mathematical hardness is entirely external.

The framework approaches the conjecture via two complementary, partial reductions. The deeper statement remains open. The sharper reduction is the jet-order reduction. It replaces Grothendieck-period machinery with a finite per-order Gröbner--Shirshov independence computation. The skein engine executes this computation natively. This pairs with a single QOU-native surreal bridge lemma. This reduction converts an external problem into an incremental research target natively structured on the framework's jet-order filtration. The second reduction is the transcendence shadow. It reduces algebraic independence to the non-collapse of the brane tower and Nesterenko-type arithmetic control of the quantum dilogarithm. Both paths relocate the difficulty. The Lean formalisation proves the structural half: the tower decomposition, Chern--Simons faithfulness, and the downstream implications (algebraic independence \Rightarrow Borel--Zagier \Rightarrow irrationality). The transcendence core is axiomatised as the Lean class HyperbolicVolumeIndependence. Following the conditional-class convention, the downstream results remain conditionally rigorous.

The conjecture serves as an ideal statement. It guarantees the predicted spectrum arises from no algebraic coincidence. As the formal-chain remark records, the mass predictions and the categorical derivation live entirely over \mathbb{Z}[q, q^{-1}]. They function independently of whether the volumes are transcendental, algebraic, or rational. The framework operates strictly on the proved numerical distinctness of the three volumes. This distinctness suffices for all mass predictions.
